function: Learned multi-agent beam hopping: each satellite selects which cells its spotbeams illuminate in every timeslot, maximizing throughput and minimizing queuing delay (p. 7).
system: Multi-beam LEO forward link, 9 satellites at 1500 km, 76 cells, up to 3 spotbeams each, single-antenna users, 11.7 GHz, 200 MHz, no RIS (pp. 3, 10).
method: Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning, QMIX with GRU agent network, mixing network and hypernetwork, double deep Q-learning; centralized offline training, distributed execution (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: free-space path loss with ITU-R S.1528 and S.465-6 antenna patterns, Poisson traffic, 76-cell region with population-based traffic; no 3GPP model or measured channels (pp. 3-4, 9, 12).
test_conditions: Trained on Poisson traffic, RT 20-100 and NRT 100-700 Mbps; tested on 100 instances per load case with limits outside that range and on population-based traffic (pp. 9, 11-12).
baselines: Non-learned only: random, periodic, queue-length-prioritized, queue-delay-prioritized and USWG [18] beam hopping; no-load-balancing and maximum-elevation association; no learned baseline (pp. 10-12).
metrics: Long-term network throughput (Mbps), long-term average queuing delay (ms), traffic load gap, number of multi-served cells, episode reward and loss, execution time (pp. 10-12).
complexity: Big-O orders for association (674 us) and model execution (957 us, about 1 ms per decision); no parameter or FLOP count (p. 12, Table VI).
q1_support: p. 3: "A wide-adopted forward channel model is used in this paper", a free-space path loss with antenna gains; p. 4: patterns follow "ITU-R S.1528". Own simulator; no 3GPP TR 38.811, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "the limit values are outside the training range, which can verify the generalization of trained QMIX model"; p. 12: "heavy traffic demands exceed the training range of QMIX".
q3_support: p. 10: "we compare the proposed method (called QMIX-BH) against five different BH schemes": random, periodic, queue-length, queue-delay and USWG [18], all non-learned; no earlier DRL beam hopping method or standard DRL algorithm is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "the model execution time is around 1 ms"; Table VI gives the big-O orders of the association and of the model execution, with 674 us and 957 us.
q5_support: p. 9: "a LEO multi-beam satellite system is simulated" with own parameters (Table II); p. 12: traffic "determined according to the population distribution in cells"; no link to code or data.
notes: Title on p. 1 matches the DOI. Area 6: the learned part is the beam hopping pattern of each satellite, a beam control of satellite links (p. 7). The above_phy check passes because learned beam control in satellite links is physical layer, although the paper calls it scheduling; the cell-satellite association (Algorithm 1, p. 6) is a non-learned iterative algorithm above the physical layer. The system check does not apply to NTN works. q2 is 1 because the paper states that the test load cases lie outside the training range (p. 11, Table IV image on p. 11), but the new conditions are traffic loads of the same constellation and channel model, so the reviewer may confirm. q1 is 0: antenna patterns follow ITU-R S.1528 and S.465-6 (p. 4) but the channel is free-space path loss in an own simulator, so the reviewer may confirm. Tables I to VI are images; Table II on p. 10 lists 11.7 GHz and 1500 km.
